example_statement: Ministry of Agriculture Crop Forecast Survey Index (CFSI) projects 40% or greater crop losses
Crop yield reduction predicted to be more than 50% based on LEAP index
Fodder deficit of 40% or more
Ignition probability equal to or greater than 70%
Observed Conditions: Relative humidity (Rh) of 45 percent or higher in the respective city where Tmax condition is met
Predicted increase in Sudd inundation extent over the next two months greater than 5% compared to seasonal minimum
River flow above 150,000 cusecs at Nowshera station of Kabul River predicted by flood bulletin C and significant flood warnings/advisories with 3-5 days lead time
One confirmed cholera case reported by EPHI in a neighbouring woreda/district of the 20 identified woredas/districts within the same country or neighboring district of bordering country
Weekly dengue caseload exceeding 1,500 cases in May, June, July, December, and January
Nino3.4 index equal or greater than 0.5K in NDJ average forecast issued in July
Weekly Extreme Forecast Index (EFI) from ECMWF model greater than 0.8
Predicted water levels of Babai and West Rapti rivers to rise to their existing danger levels at Chepang and Kusum stations respectively within next 48 hours
Vulnerability Assessment Analysis report issued in January projects 20% of the population in drought-induced IPC Phase 3 and 4 in January
Category 3 – 30% or higher excess mortality (ranging upwards as high as 45% to 65% excess daily mortality)
Trigger threshold: Category 3 with predicted excess mortality of 45% or higher
If first trigger not activated, activation requires IBF model detection of drought by April and official drought declaration by Government of Zimbabwe

Numerical weather prediction (NWP) or special weather advisories predict extreme and widespread rainfall for next three days across Babai and West Rapti basin areas and districts, provided rivers are flowing at stage level less than 2m below existing danger level
Forecast of cold wave with a lead time of 4 days
72-hour forecast confirmation with at least 75% probability of cold wave occurrence
Day temperature exceeding 39.5°C in the North for 4 consecutive days during July-August
Region-specific temperature thresholds for Orange level: Northern Kazakhstan -40°C, Akmola -40°C, Kostanay -40°C, Pavlodar -40°C, Eastern Kazakhstan (including Abay) -40°C, Karaganda -35°C
Heat Index corresponds to more than 90th percentile values for summer months (March-May)
Forecast lead time maximum 5 days including 3 days heatwave duration
Forecast Criteria: DHM issues a red alert heatwave bulletin ('take action') for the next 3 days in the target city or its associated district
72-hour forecast used to confirm heatwave occurrence
Heatwave occurrence probability with 72-hour lead time less than 75% triggers stop mechanism
Forecast Criteria: Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) from DHM forecasts daily maximum temperature above the 99th percentile threshold in the target city/municipality for the next 3 consecutive days
Maximum day temperature forecast of 2°C or less
Expected maximum temperature higher than the 95th percentile of monthly historical maximum temperatures for June-September (2000-2024)
7-day temperature forecast minimum below -40°C (-35°C in Karaganda region) with precipitation and increased wind speed persisting for at least two days in any district
Significant increase in internal volcanic activity parameters such as seismicity, gas emissions, deformation
Eruptive event with explosive index VEI 3 and ash fall exceeding 2 mm as per ASH3D model (Special Report C)

Level 2 (orange alert) bulletin received four days before impact, triggered by anomalies such as second-level seismic crisis, second-level micro-deformation of the ground, and changes in gas composition (carbon dioxide accumulation) persisting for several hours a day
At least two models among BMD, IMD, ECMWF, GFS, JTWC forecast wind speeds of 125 km/h or greater in coastal districts of Bangladesh with a lead time of 72 hours or more
Category 4 or 5 cyclone within 250 km of Fiji
